children: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, Financials), the parent company of Google, is expanding its health approach with a multiyear relationship and strategic investment in Flo Health, a major women's health app.
And starting in early 2027, customers will be able to link Flo to Google Health.

The connection would bring Fitbit data like sleep, heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin temperature and respiration rate into Flo. The aim is to enhance cycle forecasts and give more individualized counsel across the life phases from menstruation and pregnancy to perimenopause.
The size of Flo makes the pairing unique. The firm estimates it has crossed 500 million downloads, and reaches more than 80 million women a month.
The two businesses also want to co-brand devices that combine Flo's algorithms and women's health knowledge with Google's wearable hardware and sensors.
For Alphabet, the potential isn't only measuring health.

A tighter integration between the Fitbit and Google Health and AI-powered coaching might make the company's wearable ecosystem more valuable and encourage more participation with tailored health services.
Privacy will be critical to the success of the strategy. The firms noted that consumers must give express approval for each sort of data sharing and can withdraw that consent at any time.
The next driver will be the launch in early 2027 and whether the integration drives larger use of Google's health and wearable devices.

title: Google Is Making a Bigger Health Bet
